svg.title: Change Data Capture (CDC)
svg.desc: Change Data Capture (CDC). Stream every committed change from the database log to other systems. Step 1, Every commit is logged: The app updates a row as usual. Before the commit returns, the change is in the transaction log. Step 2, Read the log, emit events: The connector tails the log from its saved position and emits each change as an event, in order. Step 3, One write, many copies: Search index, cache and warehouse each apply the event at their own pace. The app wrote only once. Step 4, Restarts and their price: While the connector is down the log piles up. It resumes from 42, so 43 arrives again: skipped.

g.text: The app updates a row as usual. Before the commit returns, the change is in the transaction log.
The connector tails the log from its saved position and emits each change as an event, in order.
Search index, cache and warehouse each apply the event at their own pace. The app wrote only once.
While the connector is down the log piles up. It resumes from 42, so 43 arrives again: skipped.
the change is appended to the log: entry 43
only then does the commit return
Why the log, not the table?
The table holds only the current state;
the log has every change, deletes included.
